newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish external reserves down 379 mln punts in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Irish external reserves down 379 mln punts in Dec.

text.p: Ireland's official external reserves fell by 379 million Irish pounds to 4.96 billion at the end of December, central bank monthly statistics showed on Thursday.
The bank said negative foreign exchange market intervention and payments of interest and principal on Exchequer foreign debt exceeded receipts from the European Union.
In addition, a valuation adjustment reduced the Irish pound value of the reserves by 34 million punts, the bank said.
The central bank supplied the money market with support amounting to 210 million punts at end-December, 384 million less than the end-November figure.
The effect of the fall in government balances was partly offset by the liquidity impact of negative foreign exchange market interventions and the seasonal increase of currency in circulation.

Credit to the government by domestic credit institutions fell by 94 million punts in December while holdings of Exchequer notes and government bonds fell by 38 million and 69 million Irish pounds respectively.
Non-residents reduced their holdings of Irish government securities by 124 million.

The combination of negative Irish-pound funding, substantial net government expenditure and payments on the exchequer foreign debt contributed to a fall of 988 million in government balances at the central bank.
